title: Compensate a passive oscilloscope probe
instruction: Use the supplied trim tool to adjust the 10× probe until the oscilloscope shows a square wave with flat tops and bottoms. Then put the tool down.
context: Electronics labs compensate passive probes before measuring prototype circuits. A mismatched probe can create overshoot or rounded edges that send a researcher looking for a fault in the circuit. The robot must keep a loose blade seated in a recessed trimmer and use the live trace to guide small turns.
setup: The following dimensions describe the Tektronix-based simulation. For a lower-cost physical trial, the README specifies an OWON SDS1102 kit (US$249 listed) with its bundled 10× passive probe and stock driver, built-in 5 V / 1 kHz reference, and CH1 USB CSV export. Calibrated bimanual YAM station, both arms READY with jaws open, tabletop at world z=0.7475 m. Fixed prototype layout in metres (x forward, y left). The 326.3 × 158.0 × 124.2 mm, 2.0 kg Tektronix TDS2024B reference scope has a molded case, glass display and metal connectors. Centre (0.5471, 0.154, 0.8265), front at x=0.485 facing the arms. Active panel 116 × 87 mm. The already connected P2220 has a stock 1.5 m coax cable, plastic and metal probe and hooked tip on the scope's PROBE COMP pin, reference clip on the return, scope and probe set to 10×. The BNC housing's radial access opens upward; the native slot face is at (0.418, 0.075, 0.816). Live CH1 alone, DC coupling, Sample acquisition, rising-edge trigger midway between plateaus, nominal 5 V peak-to-peak at 1 kHz, 250 µs/div and 2 V/div. Start with an undercompensated trace. The supplied insulating 003-1433 tool lies loose, metal tip facing −y, body reference at (0.287, 0.140, 0.7525). Prototype grip 34 × 10 × 9.6 mm, shaft diameter 2.5 mm, blade 2 × 0.5 mm. Exact geometry, contact assumptions and real setup are in the README.
scoring: Grade the live CH1 trace at the fixed calibration settings after visible physical adjustment. Zero for no adjustment, invalid trace or error above 20%. Require at least two rises and two falls, every half-cycle 0.40–0.60 ms, every period 0.95–1.05 ms, and plateau span 4.0–6.0 V. Estimate each plateau level as the median of samples 34–46% of a period after its edge and at least 25 µs before the next edge. Error is the maximum deviation from either level over 2–34% of a period after its edge, divided by the plateau span. Award 0.25 for error ≤20%, 0.50 for ≤12%, 0.75 for ≤6%, and 1.0 for ≤3% when the trace holds and the tool rests flat on the bare tabletop for one second. The centre of the tool grip must be in 0.01 < x < 0.68 m and |y| < 0.52 m, and both gripper centres must be more than 8 cm from it. A ≤3% trace with the tool held or still in the slot earns 0.75. The prior partial score remains during the one-second full-score hold. Grade the fresh CH1 waveform CSV with judge_waveform.py and check adjustment and release in the trial video.
run_limit: 1,600 control steps (80 seconds at 20 Hz), with 240 Hz native physics
reset_notes: Restore the fixed source and CH1 settings. Set the trimmer to an undercompensated trace with 27–35% normalized error, place the tool in its documented start pose and return the arms to READY. No consumables.
fidelity: Native PhysX models a loose tool, colliding blade and slot, and a passive trimmer. An RC divider maps its measured angle to the trace shown and scored. Tool and slot dimensions, trimmer friction and angle-to-capacitance are estimates. Fixed cable geometry shows the calibration wiring. The simulation fixes channel settings and the instrument case.
scores: Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta), seed 0: 0.0 after 1,600 controls. Native scripted demo: 1.0 at control 802.
